tagline: Down the White River, up to a 58-degree cave.
intro: From the White River bridge at Calico Rock the byway follows the river south through Optimus to Allison, then winds west on Highway 14 into the Sylamore District of the Ozark National Forest, about 26 miles in all. It ends on Forest Road 1110 at Blanchard Springs.

There in 1940 a Civilian Conservation Corps crew dammed the creek that runs out of the spring and made Mirror Lake, with an observation shelter of their building nearby. The spring's water comes out of the cave at the same temperature all year.
season: Early spring for the dogwoods and redbuds in the white oak-hickory woods, or fall for the color.

moments.title: Calico Rock
moments.text: A town on the north bank of the White River, named by pioneers for a colorful rock formation they thought looked like calico cloth.

moments.title: Sylamore Creek Bridge
moments.text: Just west of Highway 9 at Allison, a county road crosses Sylamore Creek on a wire-cable suspension bridge of 1945, one of three known in Arkansas.

moments.title: Blanchard Springs Caverns
moments.text: Locals in the 1930s knew it as Half-Mile Cave, and guided tours now reach all three of its levels, where the cave holds at 58 degrees the year round.
